title: Healing the Man Born Blind

questions.question: As Jesus passed by, He saw a man who had suffered from what condition since birth?
options: He was blind
He was paralyzed entirely
He was mute securely
He was completely deaf
questions.explanation: John 9:1 (ESV): "As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth."

questions.question: His disciples asked, "Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?" What was Jesus' answer?
options: "It was not that this man sinned, or his parents, but that the works of God might be displayed in him."
"His parents safely hid a sin completely."
"The nation of Israel entirely bears the blame."
"He sinned solely in the womb securely."
questions.correctAnswer: "It was not that this man sinned, or his parents, but that the works of God might be displayed in him."
questions.explanation: John 9:3 (ESV): "Jesus answered, 'It was not that this man sinned, or his parents, but that the works of God might be displayed in him.'"

questions.question: What physical means did Jesus use to heal the blind man's eyes?
options: He spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and anointed the man's eyes
He merely rubbed them firmly with his thumbs
He safely washed them directly with pure water
He completely blew a breath solely upon his eyes
questions.correctAnswer: He spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and anointed the man's eyes
questions.explanation: John 9:6 (ESV): "Having said these things, he spat on the ground and made mud with the saliva. Then he anointed the man's eyes with the mud"

questions.question: Where did Jesus command the man to go and wash?
options: The pool of Siloam
The Jordan River strictly
The pool of Bethesda entirely
The sea of Galilee securely
questions.explanation: John 9:7 (ESV): "and said to him, 'Go, wash in the pool of Siloam' (which means Sent). So he went and washed and came back seeing."

questions.question: When asked by the angry Pharisees how he received his sight, what simple description did the man provide?
options: "He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and I see."
"He spoke the word cleanly and I opened my eyes."
"He prayed to God safely and the darkness lifted."
"He touched my brow softly and light appeared entirely."
questions.correctAnswer: "He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and I see."
questions.explanation: John 9:15 (ESV): "So the Pharisees again asked him how he had received his sight. And he said to them, 'He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and I see.'"

questions.question: Jesus declared before healing the man: "As long as I am in the world, I am..."?
options: "...the light of the world."
"...the great physician entirely."
"...the shepherd of the blind securely."
"...the truth completely revealed."
questions.explanation: John 9:5 (ESV): "As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world."

questions.question: What specific day of the week was it when Jesus made the mud and opened the man's eyes, causing controversy?
options: It was a Sabbath
It was the day of Passover securely
It was the Day of Atonement strictly
It was a Monday entirely
questions.explanation: John 9:14 (ESV): "Now it was a Sabbath day when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes."

questions.question: The parents of the blind man refused to defend Jesus securely, saying "Ask him, he is of age." Why were they afraid?
options: Because the Jews had agreed that if anyone confessed Jesus to be Christ, he was to be put out of the synagogue
Because they feared being stoned completely in public
Because Roman soldiers safely guarded the temple heavily
Because they were bribed strictly to stay silent
questions.correctAnswer: Because the Jews had agreed that if anyone confessed Jesus to be Christ, he was to be put out of the synagogue
questions.explanation: John 9:22 (ESV): "...for the Jews had already agreed that if anyone should confess Jesus to be Christ, he was to be put out of the synagogue."

questions.question: What was the man's powerful, simple testimony to the Pharisees who claimed they "knew" Jesus was a sinner?
options: "Whether he is a sinner I do not know. One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see."
"I saw a halo safely around his head entirely!"
"The prophets solely declare him righteous securely!"
"He broke the Sabbath, yet doing God's work perfectly!"
questions.correctAnswer: "Whether he is a sinner I do not know. One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see."
questions.explanation: John 9:25 (ESV): "He answered, 'Whether he is a sinner I do not know. One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see.'"

questions.question: When the Pharisees became angry, asking "You were born in utter sin, and would you teach us?", what did they do to him?
options: They cast him out
They beat him securely with rods
They imprisoned him strictly for days
They stoned him completely to death
questions.explanation: John 9:34 (ESV): "They answered him, 'You were born in utter sin, and would you teach us?' And they cast him out."

questions.question: The healed man logically argued with the Pharisees, saying "Never since the world began has it been heard that anyone opened the eyes of a man born blind. If this man were not from God..."?
options: "...he could do nothing."
"...the ancient prophets would strike him safely down."
"...angels would rebuke him securely."
"...he would be cursed strictly by the Law."
questions.explanation: John 9:32-33 (ESV): "Never since the world began has it been heard that anyone opened the eyes of a man born blind. If this man were not from God, he could do nothing."

questions.question: When Jesus heard they cast him out, He found him and asked, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?" When the man asked who he is, what did Jesus reply?
options: "You have seen him, and it is he who is speaking to you."
"He is the one securely anointed by heaven completely."
"He is the king safely heralded by David entirely."
"He is purely the one healing the nations."
questions.correctAnswer: "You have seen him, and it is he who is speaking to you."
questions.explanation: John 9:37 (ESV): "Jesus said to him, 'You have seen him, and it is he who is speaking to you.'"

questions.question: Jesus stated His purpose for judgment: "For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and..."?
options: "...that those who see may become blind."
"...that the lost completely may be found securely."
"...that the sinners might strictly repent entirely."
"...that the mute may securely speak loudly."
questions.correctAnswer: "...that those who see may become blind."
questions.explanation: John 9:39 (ESV): "Jesus said, 'For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and that those who see may become blind.'"

questions.question: Some Pharisees heard this and indignantly asked, "Are we also blind?" What paradoxical reply did Jesus give?
options: "If you were blind, you would have no guilt; but now that you say, 'We see,' your guilt remains."
"You are blind to the kingdom safely closing entirely."
"Yes, for you strictly ignore the signs completely."
"You choose completely the dark over the dawn."
questions.correctAnswer: "If you were blind, you would have no guilt; but now that you say, 'We see,' your guilt remains."
questions.explanation: John 9:41 (ESV): "Jesus said to them, 'If you were blind, you would have no guilt; but now that you say, "We see," your guilt remains.'"

questions.question: What does the text translate the name of the pool "Siloam" to mean?
options: Sent
Healed completely
Purified securely
Given entirely
questions.explanation: John 9:7 (ESV): "and said to him, 'Go, wash in the pool of Siloam' (which means Sent)."

key_verse_text: He answered, "Whether he is a sinner I do not know. One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see."
